Och, sure there's always lights movin' about on the hills of a night. May be poitín men tendin' their stills — best not go askin' after that too loudly, mind. Or mayhap it was just someone walkin' late with a lantern, takin' a shortcut home from the public house.

Of course, there's them that'd say 'twas the sídhe, the fairy folk stirrin'. I wouldn't go chasin' after such lights if I were ye, mo chara — whether 'tis fairies or distillers, neither one wants to be found.
